counterfactual_missing_items: Negative results for hepatitis, antinuclear antibodies, rheumatoid factor, heparin-induced thrombocytopenia antibodies, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
decisive_items: Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Hypercellular marrow consisting of 80% plasma cells with atypical morphology and κ-light-chain restriction
response.rationale: The presence of abnormal paraprotein bands, monoclonal IgG-κ protein, and hypercellular marrow with plasma cell infiltration strongly supports the diagnosis of multiple myeloma, while the absence of other conditions and the presence of lytic bony lesions further confirm this diagnosis

rejected.why: Although the patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and cryoprotein precipitate, the overall clinical and laboratory findings are more consistent with multiple myeloma
